map.输入 0–5 岁儿童的年龄、性别、身高/体重/头围，对照 WHO 生长标准曲线评: Enter the age, sex and height/weight/head circumference of a child aged 0-5, and assess growth percentile and trend against the WHO growth standard curves. For child health monitoring and developmental delay screening.
map.定期体检录入：每次儿保把身高/体重（2 岁后加 BMI）录入，对照 WHO 同月: Regular check-up entry: at each well-child visit enter height/weight (plus BMI after age 2), compare against the WHO P3-P97 reference interval for the same age in months, and see which percentile the baby falls in.
map.追 longitudinal 趋势：单次数值意义有限，连续多次落在同一百分位带（: Track the longitudinal trend: a single reading has limited meaning; staying within the same percentile band across several visits (for example stable near P50) is healthy; a short-term drop across bands needs checks for feeding or disease.
map.个体化解读：高个子父母宝宝常居 P85 以上、小个子父母常居 P15 以下，均可: Individualized interpretation: babies of tall parents often sit above P85 and those of short parents below P15, both can be normal; the key is whether the 'genetic track' is stable.
map.男、12 月、身高 75.7cm、体重 9.6kg: Male, 12 months, height 75.7 cm, weight 9.6 kg
: WHO reference for boys at 12 months: height [68.6, 71.0, 75.7, 80.0, 82.5] cm, weight [7.7, 8.6, 9.6, 10.8, 11.8] kg. Height 75.7 = P50 median (average); weight 9.6 = P50 median (average). A height of 80 cm falls into P85, upper middle. BMI is only assessed from 24 months of age.
map.百分位低就一定有问题吗？: Does a low percentile always mean a problem?
map.不一定。P3–P15 且长期稳定、沿自身轨道增长，多为遗传偏矮，无需干预；仅当: Not necessarily. A child between P3 and P15 who is stable long term and growing along their own track is usually constitutionally short and needs no intervention; only a value <P3 or a clear short-term drop warrants medical assessment of nutrition or endocrine status. Focus on 'growth velocity' rather than a single absolute value.
map.WHO 标准和我国标准差多少？: How much do the WHO standard and the Chinese standard differ?
map.我国 2009 与 2015 生长标准与 WHO 高度接近（均基于健康母乳喂养人: China's 2009 and 2015 growth standards are very close to WHO (both based on healthy breastfed populations). This tool uses the WHO 0-5 year standard: birth weight 2.5-4.0 kg is normal, monthly gain 1-1.5 kg for the first 3 months, 0.5-0.6 kg at 3-6 months, 0.25-0.3 kg at 6-12 months, and 2.5-3 kg over the whole year at 1-2 years.
